dependencies: Gaussian polar decomposition and standard Gaussian/radial moments
proofs.full_local_argument: Let v be uniform on the unit sphere of a k-dimensional subspace, k>=1, and let ||x||<=R, R>0. Write P for orthogonal projection onto that subspace. With g standard Gaussian in R^k, g=S u where u is uniform on the sphere, S=||g|| and S,u are independent. Gaussian even moments and radial integration give E g1^(2ell)=(2ell-1)!! and E S^(2ell)=k(k+2)...(k+2ell-2). Thus by rotational invariance, E<v,x>^(2ell)=||Px||^(2ell)(2ell-1)!!/[k(k+2)...(k+2ell-2)]<=R^(2ell)(2ell-1)!!/k^ell. Odd moments vanish by symmetry. Since |<v,x>|<=R, the exponential power series may be integrated term by term; using (2ell-1)!!/(2ell)!=1/(2^ell ell!) yields E exp(t<v,x>)<=exp(t^2 R^2/(2k)) for all real t. For a>0, Markov's inequality with t=ka/R^2 gives P{<v,x>>a}<=exp(-ka^2/(2R^2)); apply the same argument to -<v,x> and sum to get P{|<v,x>|>a}<=2exp(-ka^2/(2R^2)). This also covers k=1. No conditioning on a selected success event is used.
map: Gaussian polar decomposition gives spherical moments.
Moment bound gives a sub-Gaussian moment-generating function.
Two-sided Chernoff bound gives the stated tail.

map: Fix an arbitrary independent algorithm seed. Pad stops with ignored feasible queries, keeping saved output. Total-feasible rules ensure ||x_t^sim||<=R and ||xhat^sim||<=R on every simulated history before any coupling is established.

Simulate query t by returning the full jet of F_t(x)=lambda[x-cv1-q sum_{i=1}^{t-1}h_tau(<vi,x>)v_{i+1}]. Then x_t^sim depends only on v1,...,v_{t-1}; the answer may additionally depend on vt; final simulated output depends only on v1,...,vN.
Define E_{t,i}={|<vi,x_t^sim>|<=tau/2} for 1<=t<=N,t<=i<=m-1; E_out={|<vm,xhat^sim>|<=tau/2}; E=E_out intersect all E_{t,i}.

Condition only on v1,...,v_{t-1}. Each remaining vi is marginally uniform on the sphere of their (d-t+1)-dimensional orthogonal complement, while x_t^sim is fixed. Lemma11.2 gives P(E_{t,i}^c)<=2exp(-(d-m)tau^2/(8R^2)). Conditioning on v1,...,vN gives the same bound for E_out^c. Independence among remaining directions or events is not required.

Since tau^2=R^2/(256m^3), an unconditional union bound over fewer than m^2+1 events gives P(E)>=1-2(m^2+1)exp(-(d-m)/(2048m^3))>=1-delta. Do NOT condition on earlier success events; their selection would invalidate the claimed unchanged spherical law.

On E, prove actual/simulated transcript equality inductively. Empty histories give the same first query. Equal histories through t-1 give the same query t; all omitted terms indexed i>=t have scalar arguments in the flat interval by E_{t,i}, so their values and every derivative vanish. Therefore full jets agree, hence histories agree through t. After N queries saved outputs agree, including early stopping.
E_out places the common output in the hidden slab. flat_chain_properties then gives r_tan>=H. This holds with probability at least 1-delta for each fixed seed; integrate over the independent seed.

Average the joint bound over frames to obtain one fixed frame with seed-only probability at least 1-delta. At delta=1/4 use H>epsilon, not H>=epsilon, to contradict per-instance success>=2/3. Nonnegativity of residual gives the expected-residual corollary by multiplying H by 1-delta.

Set R=D/2. Section11.3 pp30–31 combines power-law inversion with its internal Lemma11.5 interface: opposite constant operators on the interval have disjoint singleton epsilon-solution endpoints and no zero-query output distribution succeeds with probability 2/3 on both. This supplies uniform normalization without inventing a parallel unpublished zero-query dependency.

assumptions: Query and output maps are measurable, defined on every transcript of the prescribed dimensions and return feasible points on every such transcript.
Algorithm uses at most N original-F calls under a worst-case cap; saved output retained when padding early-stopped runs.
Queries are bounded by the public ball; no unbounded outside-ball probes.
statement.conclusion: The joint and fixed-frame residual probability bounds hold with the exact threshold H. Also E_{V,xi}r_tan(xhat)>=(1-delta)H, and the same expected-residual conclusion holds for a fixed frame satisfying the seed-only probability bound. At delta=1/4 and H STRICTLY greater than epsilon, some fixed frame has failure probability at least 3/4, contradicting a per-instance success guarantee >=2/3. Consequently T_p^rand(epsilon;Lp,D;success>=2/3)=Omega_p((LpD^p/epsilon)^(2/(3p-1))) with dimension allowed to grow. This concerns a worst-case query cap, not an expected query budget.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Use the fully specified eta/chi/rho/h_tau and T_V,F_V construction of flat_chain_properties: X=B_2^d(R),x0=0,m=N+1,q=1-1/(2m),c=R/(2sqrt(m)),tau=R/(16m^(3/2)),Bp=max{1,||rho^(p-1)||infinity},lambda=Lp tau^(p-1)/Bp. V is uniform over orthonormal m-frames in R^d, drawn once before the run. Algorithm seed xi is independent of V. A call returns the entire jet (F,DF,...,D^(p-1)F). Let H=LpR^p/[8Bp16^(p-1)m^((3p-1)/2)].
statement.parameter_domains: As above; delta is a failure-probability parameter, unrelated to upper-solver accuracy. Set R=D/2 for diameter complexity; p-dependent constants assume fixed p.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such randomized algorithm, with frame distribution fixed before the run independently of its seed, P_{V,xi}{r_tan(xhat)>=H}>=1-delta. For that algorithm there exists some fixed V with P_xi{r_tan(xhat)>=H | V}>=1-delta. The hard fixed frame need not be common to all algorithms.
